messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [SEV2] Dedicated pool 'delta-enterprise-vpc' GPU utilization 98% — sustained queue depth rising. Autoscaler at max. Queueing: 1.8k reqs. Affected: deltacorp (single-tenant). AlertID: INC-2026-042
maya (oncall): paging, I'm on it. Have handoff? :hand:
ops-shift: I'm seeing long tail latencies, p99 > 6s, rate steady at 420 rps. GPU memory pressure 98%. No OOMs yet, but queuing increasing.
maya (oncall): Can we trigger burst reserve? What's remaining capacity in region us-west-2?
kevin (platform-ops): us-west-2 has 12 spare GPUs in general pool but not in delta's dedicated pool. Burst requires tenant approval + billing. I can request fast-burst but need product/cs sign-off.
anna (cust-success): pinging Jon (customer). Jon.delta, are you okay with temporary burst? We'll need authorization to spin reserved GPUs under your contract.
jon.delta: We're impacted — API latency spikes causing timeouts for our UI flows. Approve temporary burst to keep service up. Please proceed, priority P0 for us.
liam (eng-runtime): If we add burst GPUs, we'll need to rebind the tenant service to the new nodes. I can run the rebind + KV-cache warmup. Expect ~2-3 min to start draining queued requests after binding.
maya (oncall): Plan: 1) Approve burst (15m provisional) 2) Platform to allocate GPUs 3) Runtime to rebind & warm KV cache 4) Monitor queue drain and rollback if errors.
kevin (platform-ops): Allocating 6 GPUs from general pool to delta tenant now (request submitted). ETA ~150s to attach.
ops-shift: Routing note — we'll keep fallback model variant (half-precision quantized) off for now to avoid quality regressions. If queue persists, we'll enable it as last resort.
liam (eng-runtime): Rebind script ready: 
```bash
# attach nodes and rebind
redwoodctl tenants attach --tenant deltacorp --pool delta-enterprise-vpc --gpus 6
redwoodctl runtime rebind --tenant deltacorp --warm-kv
``` 
I'll run after kevin confirms attached.
kevin (platform-ops): GPUs attached, hostnames: gpu-attach-12..17. Confirmed in infra: delta-enterprise-pool size increased.
liam (eng-runtime): Starting rebind now. Monitoring logs.
liam (eng-runtime): KV warmup started, streaming logs: "warm_kv: 12% -> 94%". Queues dropping.
ops-shift: p99 dropped from 6.2s -> 1.1s in last minute. Queue depth 1.8k -> 420.
maya (oncall): Customer reported improvement? @jon.delta
jon.delta: UI looks normal again. No timeouts. Thanks team.
anna (cust-success): Noting customer approval in ticket CS-7891. Will follow up for billing reconciliation.
maya (oncall): We'll keep burst for 15m then evaluate. If queue stable, drain remaining and release GPUs. Anyone want to own post-mortem? Suggest eng-runtime + platform ops.
liam (eng-runtime): I'll own the technical AAR. Platform ops — can you provide allocation timeline + why autoscaler hit max replicas?
kevin (platform-ops): Will capture metrics and the autoscaler config. Early note: tenant's sustained token load > configured autoscale max replicas (6). Suggest raising target for enterprise tenants or add reserved burst comms.
maya (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Monitoring window open for 30m. Closing paging in 10.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 marked mitigated by maya at 1764510442. Postmortem assigned to liam, kevin. CS ticket linked: CS-7891.
liam (eng-runtime): Quick note for AAR: consider autoscaler policy change: allow emergency burst to borrow from region pool automatically if customer has approved burst in contract UI.
kevin (platform-ops): Agreed. I'll draft recommended change and cost/guardrails.
anna (cust-success): I'll collect customer timeline and add to postmortem. Jon, we'll schedule a debrief after AAR.
jon.delta: Appreciate the fast action. We'll review usage patterns and might request higher reserved capacity.
maya (oncall): Thanks all. Handing off active monitoring to ops-shift for 30m. If anything flares, re-ping #incidents.
ops-shift: Ack, monitoring. Keeping logs open.
